source_name: Наші Гроші (nashigroshi.org) — procurement investigative journalism
why_relevant: Investigative outlet covering state-bank procurement; produced the reporting linking Oschadbank contracts to BMS Consulting including World Bank debarment context. Useful for reputational/red-flag layer on integrators and for surfacing contracts that the parties do not publicise.

source_name: UKRCARD (ПЦ УКРКАРТ) — integration products
why_relevant: Ukrainian processing centre publishing its integration product line (UAPI etc.) for bank-side connection. Ukrcard-adjacent integrators must build to these interfaces, so the page is both a competitor datapoint and a pointer to the technical partner ecosystem around UA card processing.

source_name: Megatrade partner locator ('де купити')
why_relevant: Ukrainian IT/AV distributor's reseller-locator listing named integrator partners (IT-Integrator among them). Distributor partner-locator pages are a reliable, under-used way to enumerate the integrator population and the brands each one carries.

source_name: Visa Ukraine Newsroom / Press Releases (visa.com.ua)
why_relevant: Visa's own Ukrainian press room is the primary channel for issuing/acquiring partnerships, co-brand launches and product rollouts with Ukrainian banks and fintechs (e.g. PrivatBank + Visa + NAVI gamer ecosystem, Dec 2025). Scheme-authored, dated, name-checks the partner bank/vendor.

source_name: Visa Corporate Global Newsroom (press releases listing)
why_relevant: Global/CEMEA-level Visa announcements that touch Ukraine (platform partnerships, Visa Acceptance Platform deals, stablecoin/crossborder pilots) often appear here and not on the local site. Useful for catching vendor-side deals (e.g. Fiserv) that then land in Ukraine.

source_name: Mastercard Newsroom EEMEA — Ukrainian-language section
why_relevant: Mastercard's EEMEA newsroom publishes Ukrainian-language press releases and research: bank co-operation deals, Digital First / cloud issuing programmes, Start Path Ukraine fintech cohorts, government MoUs (Ministry of Economy 'Зроблено в Україні', national cashback). Directly names partner banks, fintechs and processors.

source_name: NBU — National payment system 'Ukrainian Payment Space' (PROSTIR) section on bank.gov.ua
why_relevant: Regulator-side page on PROSTIR: governance, statistics, membership conditions. Bilingual (uk/en) and more stable than the scheme marketing site; the authoritative statement of scheme rules and counts.

source_name: NBU oversight reports (Report on oversight of payment infrastructure)
why_relevant: Periodic oversight reports give scheme-level volumes/shares (Visa vs Mastercard vs PROSTIR), participant counts and processor structure — the quantitative backbone for the switching-infrastructure view.

source_name: UnionPay International — Newsroom / Company News
why_relevant: UPI's own newsroom documents its Ukrainian market entry (NBU payment business licence 2018), acquiring launch with PrivatBank, acceptance footprint numbers (merchants/ATMs/QuickPass POS) and first local issuance. Only scheme-side record of the UnionPay leg of the UA switching landscape.

source_name: Visa Global Registry of Service Providers (periodic PDF/portal)
why_relevant: The scheme's own list of registered, PCI-DSS-validated agents/service providers, published as a dated global PDF. Filterable by country to reveal which processors, gateways, TPPs and terminal/software vendors are Visa-registered for Ukraine — the closest thing to a certified-vendor list a scheme publishes openly.

source_name: Mastercard Compliant Service Provider list (CSPCDP)
why_relevant: Mastercard's equivalent registry of PCI-compliant registered service providers; cross-referencing it with Visa's registry gives a two-scheme view of which vendors are certified to touch card data for Ukrainian acquirers/issuers.

source_name: PaySpace Magazine Ukraine (psm7.com) — payments trade press
why_relevant: Payments-native Ukrainian trade outlet that reliably re-reports scheme press releases, NBU issuing/acquiring rule changes, and publishes overview pieces enumerating Ukraine's processing centres — an efficient pointer layer over scheme and regulator primary sources.

source_name: Ministry of Economy of Ukraine — Mastercard/Visa government partnership announcements
why_relevant: State-side confirmation of scheme MoUs (digital partnership, 'Зроблено в Україні' national cashback) — these MoUs pull banks, processors and acquirers into implementation roles, so the ministry text often names the delivery partners.

source_name: Issuer/acquirer bank press centres as scheme-partnership mirrors (e.g. PrivatBank, Ukrgasbank, ASVIO Bank)
why_relevant: Banks publish the counterpart of every scheme announcement, often with more product detail (e.g. Ukrgasbank's first PROSTIR–UnionPay co-badged card; PrivatBank's UnionPay acquiring launch; ASVIO Bank's Visa strategic partnership). Best evidence for co-branding and issuing/acquiring partnerships.

source_name: Wikipedia (uk) — ПРОСТІР (платіжна система) and Український процесінговий центр
why_relevant: Cheap actor-map bootstrap: year-by-year list of banks that joined PROSTIR, card-in-circulation figures, and a footnote trail back to NBU primary documents. Use strictly as a pointer, never as a cited fact.

source_name: Minfin company profiles & news feeds (minfin.com.ua/company/mastercard)
why_relevant: Aggregated per-company news timeline plus legal identifiers (ЄДРПОУ, МФО, реквізити) for scheme entities registered in Ukraine — useful for tying a scheme's local legal entity to registry records.

source_name: Kyivstar/Uklon–Visa Acceptance Platform announcement (GlobeNewswire syndication)
why_relevant: Concrete 2026 example of Visa's acceptance/gateway technology being adopted by a large Ukrainian non-bank merchant platform — evidence of scheme-owned vendor stack displacing local gateways. Wire syndication makes these findable when the scheme's own site does not carry them.

source_name: Checkbox / fiscalisation certification blog — certified POS terminal models in Ukraine
why_relevant: Reveals-indirectly: Ukrainian fiscalisation/PRRO providers publish which terminal hardware (Verifone, Newland) and which integrator (e.g. SSI) passed certification — a proxy for the certified terminal-vendor landscape that the schemes themselves do not publish locally.

source_name: Ekonomichna Pravda long-form on PROSTIR ('Своя платіжна система')
why_relevant: Analytical journalism on why PROSTIR under-performs against Visa/Mastercard, with named participants, processor economics and interchange context — good for the competitive framing of the national switch versus international schemes.

source_name: LiqPay (PrivatBank) — product, docs and integration pages
why_relevant: Largest Ukrainian online acquiring gateway, tied to PrivatBank (dominant acquirer). Product pages, tariffs, API docs and CMS plugin list reveal competitive positioning, merchant segments served and channel partners.

source_name: Fondy — corporate site, partner program and resources/case studies
why_relevant: Fondy operates a formal tiered partner program (Silver/Gold/Platinum, 10-20% profit share) targeting ePOS companies, ISOs, IT integrators and agencies — an explicit channel-partner structure and a named-partner pointer set. Resources section carries customer stories.

source_name: WayForPay — site, knowledge base and integration catalogue
why_relevant: Major Ukrainian PSP; publishes its own market-share analytics (naming Fondy ~26.6%, Portmone ~21.1%, iPay ~17% as closest competitors), an integrated-services list, CMS modules and vertical solutions (restaurants, taxi, QR terminal). It also holds an NBU payment-services licence — a competitor, vendor and channel hub at once.

source_name: Portmone Business — internet acquiring product site
why_relevant: Portmone is a top-3 online payment player by WayForPay's own analytics, with both a consumer bill-payment franchise and B2B internet acquiring plus mobile payment solutions sold to banks — i.e. simultaneously a competitor and a vendor to banks.

source_name: PSP Platon — Ukrainian internet acquiring provider
why_relevant: Independent PSP positioning on PCI DSS security/compliance; a competitor whose product and compliance messaging indicates which merchant verticals and risk profiles it targets.

source_name: iPay.ua — payment service and partner integrations
why_relevant: Top-5 Ukrainian online payment service (~17% share per WayForPay analytics). Announces integration partnerships — e.g. with Vchasno.Kasa combining online acquiring with fiscalisation — a direct example of PSP+software channel partnership.

source_name: Tranzzo — white-label payment gateway
source_subtype: payment technology vendor site + vendor-hosted case study
why_relevant: White-label gateway selling to banks/PSPs (50+ payment methods, 30+ currencies, integrations with many Ukrainian banks) — a direct competitor to bank-facing payment technology vendors and an internationalising Ukrainian player. Third-party case study published by Google Cloud gives an independently-hosted account of its architecture.

source_name: Concord Fintech Solutions — open fintech ecosystem (processing, acquiring, billing)
why_relevant: Ecosystem built around the former Concord Bank comprising a processing centre, acquiring and billing; explicitly positions on 'cooperation instead of competition' with banks and retail. Central to the Concord-linked processor cluster named in the cell scope.

source_name: MustPay — product/software arm of the Concord ecosystem
why_relevant: Describes itself as developer of all products in the Concord Fintech Solutions infrastructure and of software for ecosystem partners — a vendor whose client list is a pointer to banks and fintechs using Concord-linked processing.
